name: Avots MCP

hlido_opinion.headline: A shipped multi-model gateway reachable over MCP — concrete, specific, and documented for six clients, with the usual gateway caveats about depending on a middleman.
hlido_opinion.body: Avots exposes 40+ AI models through a single MCP endpoint, so a Claude, Cursor, Cline or openclaw session can call GPT-5, DeepSeek, Sonar, Veo, Kling, ElevenLabs and others without leaving the client. What makes this reviewable rather than aspirational is specificity: sixteen named tools are listed with what each does and which are free (check_balance, list_models, check_job, calendar and avatar listing), the transport is stated precisely (streamable HTTP, MCP spec 2025-06-18, bearer auth), OAuth is supported for Claude web so there is no token copy-paste, and there is a per-client setup guide for six different clients. The generative range is unusually broad for one endpoint — chat, image, video, audio, face swap, talking avatars, lipsync, vlogs, montage. The trade-offs are inherent to the pattern: every call is routed through a third party, so the vendor sees prompts and outputs and becomes a single point of failure; the surface shows no pricing detail, uptime record, rate limits, or data-handling policy in what we captured; and there is no adoption evidence or third-party validation. A two-step confirmation on video generation is a sensible guard against expensive accidental calls and worth noting.

tier_rationale: STEADY (72) because this is shipped and specific rather than promised: sixteen named tools with free/paid status, a precisely stated transport (streamable HTTP, MCP spec 2025-06-18, bearer auth), OAuth for Claude web, and setup guides for six clients. Held below VITAL because the gateway pattern concentrates prompts, outputs and availability in one third party, and the captured surface shows no pricing detail, uptime record, rate limits or data-handling policy — the disclosures that would make that concentration acceptable.
what_it_does_well: Sixteen tools listed by name with function and free/paid status — no ambiguity about what you get
One MCP endpoint reaches 40+ models across chat, image, video, audio and avatar generation
Precise transport disclosure: streamable HTTP, MCP spec 2025-06-18, Authorization bearer
OAuth support for Claude.ai web — connect without copy-pasting a token
Per-client setup guides for Claude web, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline and openclaw
Two-step confirmation on video generation — a sensible guard against costly accidental calls
what_it_fails_at: Every request routes through a third party that sees prompts and outputs; no data-handling or retention policy on the captured surface
Single point of failure — if the gateway is down, all 40+ models are unreachable from the client
No pricing detail, rate limits, or uptime/reliability record published on the MCP page
No adoption numbers, named users, or third-party validation
Model availability depends on upstream providers; nothing states what happens when one is withdrawn
best_for: Developers who want many models available inside one MCP client without managing separate provider keys
Multimodal work (image, video, audio, avatar) reachable from a chat or IDE session
Quick experimentation across models where per-provider onboarding is the friction
not_recommended_for: Work with confidential prompts where routing through an intermediary is unacceptable
Production systems needing an SLA, published rate limits, or direct provider relationships
Buyers who require a stated data-retention and processing policy before sending anything
